I want to argue with you about something you said. The Almanackers keep growing in my head and I cannot tell whether that is because they are interesting or because they are easy. They have the clocks, they have the apprentices, they have a reason to lie about the tide clocks. That is three engines in one body and it feels like cheating. Here is everyone who currently has a claim:

1. the Bell-Wardens
2. the Marrow Guild
3. the Almanackers
4. the Keel-Chandlers
5. the Gaugers
6. the Wrackfolk
7. the Tidewrights

Give me the version of this that is worse but truer.

I would keep two of those and lose the rest, and I would lose them for the same reason: they name a thing the reader will already have understood from the scene.

1. Keep the map out of the front matter and let a character draw one badly — the reader gets the scale and the unreliability at once.
2. Put the error in the bell rather than the calculation — a mechanical fault is harder to blame anyone for, which is worse.

Write the scene, not the system. If the system is wrong the scene will tell you.
